Axiom Records

The numbers government statistical agencies published, kept at first print, with provenance, revision history, and a stable address for every fact. Records keeps each value as published; it never reconciles, imputes, or models one.

Axiom Rules · executable law

Computable law for all.

Open, machine-readable encodings of the world's rules, starting with tax and benefit policy. Cited, time-aware, and executable, so anyone can run, audit, or reform them.

Explore the lawBrowse the encoded lawAll of Axiom

households checked against five outside engines
axiom.org/oracles · 22 Sep 2026

Calculators that audit themselves

Tax software, benefit estimators, eligibility tools: all running off the same encoding, all able to point at the statute behind any number.

Ground truth for AI

People keep asking models policy questions. Verifiable answers grounded in actual law, useful for both training and inference.

Reform without rewriting

Change a parameter, re-run the calculation. Compare current law against any proposed amendment without touching the surrounding rules.

Government in plain sight

Every value cites its source. Every formula is open. Anyone can read the law, run it, and check that the answer follows.

Journal

An append-only log of accepted facts, each with its first-print date and its acceptance date.

Store

Axiom Microcosm · synthetic economy

A nation is millions of people, households, and firms. We build a synthetic one that stands in for them all.

Synthetic households for all.

Synthetic households, firms and the flows between them, calibrated to public totals from survey and administrative data: realistic enough to model tax and benefit policy for everyone, or to stand in for a population wherever one is needed, private by construction, and improved in the open.

See how it worksLatest release, in the mockAll of Axiom
95.7%
of 5,659 published targets hit within 10%
huggingface.co/datasets/policyengine/populace-us · 22 Sep 2026

The support

Which records exist and what they carry: a spine of observed survey records, completed by draws from the population's conditional distribution.

The totals

Weights that hit administrative facts: calibration against thousands of hierarchical targets, with hard weight-ratio bounds.

The economy

The same target surface on a fraction of the records, so the file is small enough to deploy.

The referee

Evaluation that scores what every operator did to the frame.

AI benchmarks for all.

policybench.org · 23 Sep 2026

PolicyBench

Testing how accurately language models calculate household taxes and benefits: 39 models, 100 households, 18 outputs each, graded against Axiom Simulator reference outputs.

EncodeBench

Can a model write the law as code? Statutes turned into cited, executable rules, scored by deterministic gates: the encoding compiles, passes CI, and contains no number the source text doesn't.

PolicyBench Draft

Can a model do the Office of Legislative Counsel's work? Deterministic evals over real congressional bill XML. Private preview, 52 cases.

resolution rule

Resolve from the registered ALFRED graph CSV for FRED series ICSA, U.S. initial unemployment insurance claims, seasonally adjusted, week ending 2026-08-15. Use the advance-vintage first print named by the resolver's releasePolicy=advance_vintage, field ICSA in the ALFRED graph CSV, multiply persons by 0.001, and round to the nearest 0.1 thousand. Later revisions do not change resolution. The generated ledger target records resolutionDate 2026-08-24 within expectedReleaseWindow 2026-08-20 through 2026-08-24; DOL weekly claims normally publish on Thursdays, so 2026-08-20 is the apparent calendar release day, but I retain the registered target date rather than changing the contract.
